summary: The design addresses real breadth and repetition problems, but several proposed behaviors are not represented in the current selector, supervised validation path, or result model. The highest risks are contract propagation, marker semantics, cache correctness, and baseline comparison granularity.

suggestions.title: Make contract presence an explicit selector mode
suggestions.rationale: `plan_tests()` currently always adds declared targets, directory mirror targets, import-impact targets, and core escalations. That contradicts the replacement semantics for a present spec contract. Add an explicit normalized contract mode: contract-present plans should use contract operands plus file-level mirror only; contract-absent plans should retain bounded fallback and emit a note.

suggestions.title: Route the spec contract through every validation entry point
suggestions.rationale: The CLI parses task files and passes `declared` into `plan_tests()`, but `ValidationSupervisor._plan_selection()` calls `plan_tests()` with no declarations, while `engine.run_validation()` only validates `task_ids`. Consequently the actual `sdd-worker`/QA background path cannot implement task declarations ∪ spec contract. Centralize index loading and pass the normalized contract and selected task declarations through engine, supervisor, CLI, and guard paths.

suggestions.title: Define a versioned index contract schema, not just a required flag
suggestions.rationale: Existing indexes use `"validation_contract": "required"`, and `check_task_graph.py` treats that value only as a missing-command policy. The kernel currently parses Markdown task commands, not a `### Validation Contract` section or cached marker operands. Specify a backward-compatible structured payload containing normalized pytest operands, marker expressions, schema version, and contract digest; reject malformed payloads rather than silently falling back.

suggestions.title: Override the default marker exclusion for explicit contract operands
suggestions.rationale: `planner.py` always appends `-m 'not e2e and not real_llm and not integration'`. Therefore an explicitly declared integration or e2e node is still deselected, even though the design says explicit operands opt into those markers. Implement deterministic per-invocation marker composition, preserving `real_llm` exclusion and linting any attempted opt-in.

suggestions.title: Use node-level evidence for cache and baseline verdicts
suggestions.rationale: `report.parse_junit()` and `SuiteResult` retain only aggregate counts; they cannot determine which test file or node was green, baseline-red, cached, or newly red. A per-file cache and baseline-aware verdict built on these aggregates can misclassify failures when an invocation contains multiple files. Persist canonical node IDs and statuses, or make the cache operate at the exact invocation/node set and fail closed when mapping is unavailable.

suggestions.title: Expand cache invalidation beyond source imports
suggestions.rationale: The proposed key covers test/source blobs, conftests, marker expression, and Python version, but pytest behavior also depends on configuration, plugins, environment variables, fixture data, generated artifacts, and collection identity. The current `ImportIndex` is AST-based and cannot observe dynamic imports or data dependencies. Include a versioned execution manifest and collection fingerprint, and treat missing/unknown inputs as cache misses.

suggestions.title: Make cache state feature-scoped and concurrency-safe
suggestions.rationale: The existing context ledger uses atomic replacement but performs unlocked read-modify-write updates. Parallel/background validations can lose one another's cache entries. Store a schema version, feature ID, base ref, contract digest, and selector version in the cache namespace; protect updates with the same file-lock pattern already used by `report.py`, and invalidate on mismatches.

suggestions.title: Implement the baseline runner as a new explicit subsystem
suggestions.rationale: The claimed reusable compiled-Cython copy mechanism is not present in the inspected worktree lifecycle code: `worktree_environment.py` resolves Git/admin and environment paths, while `worktree_manager.py` manages Git worktrees but does not copy `.so` artifacts. Baseline execution needs an explicit, tested preparation contract, identical interpreter/plugin environment, collection handling for branch-only tests, and fail-closed `unknown` results.

suggestions.title: Default feature closeout to a fresh contract run
suggestions.rationale: `/sdd-done` currently invokes the final feature run with `--no-ledger`, which only disables escalation-ledger writes; a new green-test cache could still make the closeout report entirely cached. Keep cache reuse for merge/task efficiency, but make feature closeout bypass it by default or expose an explicit fresh-run mode and report cached tests separately.

suggestions.title: Resolve brief-flow scope before making the contract universal
suggestions.rationale: Brief indexes support `type: brief`, base branches `main`, `dev`, or `staging`, and task IDs such as `HOTFIX-*`, while `ValidationSupervisor` accepts only `TASK-*` IDs and defaults selection to `origin/dev`. Either explicitly exclude `/sdd-brief` from this feature or update ID validation, index resolution, and base-ref propagation together; otherwise the all-phases claim will fail for the existing brief flow.

suggestions.title: Add end-to-end tests for selection, cache, baseline, and CI assumptions
suggestions.rationale: Current tests cover parser shape, aggregate JUnit counts, mirror selection, and escalation-ledger behavior, but not contract replacement, explicit integration/e2e selection, supervised task declaration propagation, node-level cache invalidation, baseline-only reds, concurrent cache writes, or branch-only baseline targets. These cases should be acceptance tests before narrowing local coverage.

suggestions.title: Make the nightly safety net an explicit package-suite matrix
suggestions.rationale: The existing CI core job invokes `pytest tests/` and the inspected workflow does not run every `packages/*/tests` tree; package-specific conftests and extras also differ. A nightly workflow should enumerate package suites, install each package's required workspace extras, preserve exit codes and JUnit artifacts per distribution, and define whether failures fail the workflow or open an external issue. Local narrowing should not depend on a CI job being able to mutate the repository ledger.
